title: Meeting Prep
description: Pull together everything you need to know before a meeting in under 5 minutes, including context, open questions, and what to accomplish.

children.text: Pull together everything the user needs to know before a meeting in under 5 minutes.

Find the meeting the user specified, or the next upcoming meeting. Extract:
- Meeting title and description
- Time and duration
- Attendees (names and roles)
- Any agenda or notes attached to the event

If the user named a person or topic ("my call with [name]", "the project sync"), match it to the nearest upcoming event.

Search any connected project management tools (Notion, Linear, Jira, etc.) using the meeting title, attendee names, and topic keywords. Look for:
- Active tasks or projects related to this meeting
- Previous meeting notes or agendas
- Outstanding action items related to the attendees
- Open decisions that might come up

Pull the most relevant 2-3 items and extract key context: status, blockers, open questions.

sections.title: Step 3: Search for Recent Communication Context

children.text:
Search any connected communication tools (Slack, email, etc.) for recent conversations about the meeting topic or attendees. Focus on the last 3-7 days. Look for:
- Decisions already made that will affect the discussion
- Blockers or tensions surfaced recently
- Requests or questions from the people in the meeting
- Tone or context that matters for how the meeting will go

Compile everything into this template:

```
# Meeting Brief: [Meeting Title]

**When:** [Date, time, duration]
**With:** [Attendee names and roles]
**Purpose:** [What this meeting is actually for, be specific]

---

## Background

[2-3 sentences of relevant context. What is the current state of the project or relationship? What has been happening recently?]

## What to Accomplish

- [Specific outcome 1, a decision, approval, or alignment]
- [Specific outcome 2]
- [Specific outcome 3 if applicable]

## Open Questions

- [Question the user should raise or be ready to answer]
- [Question]

## Relevant Context

**From project tools:**
[Key task or project status, blockers, or decisions relevant to this meeting]

**From recent communication:**
[Recent conversation highlights, decisions, tensions, or context that matters]

## Prep Notes

[Anything worth knowing walking in: tone to expect, likely pushback, or a decision that is about to come up]
```
Present the brief inline in chat. If the user wants a saved copy, write it to their notes folder with a filename like `[date]-[meeting-name]-brief.md`.

- **Specificity is credibility.** Name every person, project, and outcome exactly. Never "the team," always the actual name.
- **One page max.** If there is more context than fits, prioritize: What to Accomplish, then Open Questions, then Relevant Context.
- **Surface conflicts.** If any source reveals a blocker, tension, or unresolved issue, call it out in Prep Notes.
- **Never fabricate.** If connected tools return nothing useful, say so in the brief. Do not fill it with generic content.
- **Never send the brief anywhere.** It is for the user's eyes only. Show it in chat.
